Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

offspring noun

also progeny, descendants, young (of animals), issue, posterity

classical

Verg. A. 1.75 (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 4.5.23 (Lewis & Short)

prōlēs, prōlis f.

noun, third declension

offspring, progeny; descendants, a race

(vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov., Hor.)

Other words

  • fētus, fētūs m. — a bringing forth, bearing; what is brought forth: young, offspring, fruit

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 3.63: quārum in fētū et in ēducātiōne labōrem cum cernimus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Leg. 1.25 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • velut āles, ab altō quae teneram prōlem prōdūxit in āëra nīdō, hortāturque sequī

    like a bird that has led her tender young out of the high nest into the air, and urges them to followOv. Met. 8.213–215

  • quārum in fētū et in ēducātiōne labōrem cum cernimus

    when we see the trouble they (the beasts) take in bearing and rearing their youngCic. Fin. 3.63 (Lewis & Short)

See also child.
